$comment: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 ComradeArt / SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later. Declared, reviewed classifications for applied-vs-intended SELinux differences. A path matching no entry here is UNRESOLVED, and UNRESOLVED blocks. Adding a glob is a reviewed change with a reason — that is the point of this being a fixture rather than a heuristic in the comparison script.

reasons./dev/*: device nodes are labelled by the kernel and udev at runtime; no archive carries them
reasons./proc/* /sys/*: virtual filesystems; labels are policy-computed, never stored
reasons./ostree/deploy/*/var/*: the deployment's mutable /var is populated on first boot by systemd-tmpfiles, not shipped
reasons./sysroot/ostree/repo/*: the ostree object store is the deployment mechanism's own state, outside the intended-context manifest's domain
reasons./etc/locale.conf /etc/vconsole.conf /etc: written by systemd-firstboot on the first boot of an installed system; the archive ships none of them
reasons./etc/issue.d/*: NetworkManager writes a per-interface issue fragment naming the interface it configured
reasons./etc/resolv.conf /etc/NetworkManager/sys: network configuration created when the installed system first configures an interface

unclassifiedNote: Two classes remain deliberately unclassified and therefore blocking. Symlink-versus-target label divergence — /etc/mtab, /home, /media, /mnt and the *.wants/*.service unit symlinks — is where matchpathcon resolves the archive's symlink by pattern while the installed system labels the object the symlink became; it is very likely benign and 'very likely' is not a classification. Everything else UNRESOLVED is a path an installed system carries that the archive manifest does not describe, and each needs a reviewed reason before it stops blocking. Widening a glob to make a count go down would be the one thing this fixture exists to prevent.
